label: prf:surreal-rate-calculus
title: Proof of surreal rate calculus
html:
All four claims reduce to order comparisons in \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon). Items (1)--(3) are immediate from the definitions and the positivity / archimedean-smallness of \varepsilon (Reeb infinitesimal). For item (4), since \delta^2 is a strictly positive standard real and \varepsilon^{-1} - \varepsilon^3 is strictly positive in the ordered field (its leading term \varepsilon^{-1} dominates any positive infinitesimal),

\delta^2 \cdot \varepsilon^{-1} - \varepsilon^3
 =  \varepsilon^{-1}\bigl(\delta^2 - \varepsilon^4\bigr) > 0,

because \delta^2 is a standard real and \varepsilon^4 is infinitesimal, so \delta^2 - \varepsilon^4 > 0 in \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon). \square
heading: Proof
